summary: Iteration 5 FleetCare — Bell days setting, Storico operator filter, Vehicle PDF. Backend pytest 14/14 new pass (test_iteration5.py) + full regression 85/85 pass across all iterations. Verified: GET/PUT /api/settings persist bell_days (7→45→restored); GET /api/notifications/today returns bell_days in payload and upcoming size grows with the window while count (overdue+today) stays constant; GET /api/audit/operators returns list of {email,name} including admin; GET /api/audit?user_email=sertrani@gmail.com narrows to admin-only entries; unknown email returns []; /api/reports/audit/excel accepts user_email; GET /api/reports/vehicle/{id}/pdf returns 200 application/pdf %PDF-magic for admin, 403 for operatore1@test.it (no export_reports), 404 for unknown id. Frontend Playwright (admin sertrani@gmail.com): /impostazioni bell-days-input fills 45 → PUT /api/settings body has bell_days:45 → toast 'Impostazioni salvate' shown → GET /api/settings returns 45; header notification-bell popover renders bell items respecting the window. /storico filter-operator dropdown populated with 10 operators including 'Titolare'; selecting admin issues GET /api/audit?user_email=... and filter-reset clears. Vehicle card history-button opens VehicleHistoryDialog; vehicle-pdf-button triggers download 'scheda_AU100DIT.pdf'. Limited user (operatore1@test.it/pass123, only manage_payments): opens history dialog but vehicle-pdf-button hidden (count=0), matching require('export_reports').
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1434 lines (up from 1324). The recommendation to split into modules (auth/users/vehicles/policy/audit/reports/notifications/storage) remains and is becoming more pressing.

vehicle_report_pdf imports reportlab classes inside the function on every request — acceptable for cold-start memory but adds ~ms overhead per call; consider top-level imports (already imported for other report endpoints).

/api/audit/operators does one find_one per distinct email to fetch user_name; for many operators this is O(N) roundtrips. Use a single aggregation ($group by user_email with $last: user_name) instead.
SettingsInput.bell_days has no explicit upper bound; a huge value (e.g. 3650) would still be accepted and iterate all vehicles ok, but consider Pydantic Field(ge=0, le=365).
notifications_today still recomputes over all vehicles per request — cache per-request or memoize briefly.
@app.on_event startup/shutdown still used (deprecated in FastAPI ≥0.109); migrate to lifespan handler.
